'''''Suam na mais''''' is a [[Philippine cuisine|Filipino]] [[corn soup]] with [[leafy vegetables]] (like [[Moringa oleifera|moringa]], [[bitter melon]], or [[Malabar spinach]] leaves), and [[pork]] and/or [[Shrimp and prawn as food|shrimp]]. It originates from the province of [[Pampanga]]. It is also known as '''''ginisang mais''''' in [[Tagalog language|Tagalog]] and '''''sinabawang mais''''' in the [[Visayan languages]]. It is served hot, usually during the [[Wet season|rainy season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Suam na Mais (Filipino Corn Soup) |url=https://www.panlasangpinoymeatrecipes.com/suam-mais-corn-soup.htm |website=Panlasang Pinoy Meaty Recipes |access-date=April 6, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=How to Cook the Best Suam na Mais (Corn Soup) |url=https://eatlikepinoy.com/best-suam-na-mais-recipe/ |website=EatLikePinoy.com |date=January 4, 2020 |access-date=April 6, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Suam na Mais |url=https://www.kawalingpinoy.com/suam-na-mais/ |website=Kawaling Pinoy |date=August 30, 2013 |access-date=April 6, 2021}}</ref>
